newsitem.title: USA: Fla citrus growers still evaluating freeze impact.
newsitem.headline: Fla citrus growers still evaluating freeze impact.

text.p: Florida citrus growers have accelerated harvesting of their fields following the hard freeze last weekend but a statewide estimate of the damage will take several more days to compile, the head of Florida Citrus Mutual said on Tuesday.

"It was pretty uniform throughout the state," said Bobby McKown, executive director of the state's largest grower cooperative. "It wasn't a tree-killer freeze like in the 1980s but we expect we'll have some juice yield loss and some box loss as well."
McKown said consumers were unlikely to see much, if any, increase in retail orange juice prices.

"There's been a lot of wholesale level discounting of juices in the past few weeks," he said. "You're going to see prices firm up and an end to discounting. But I don't see any real changes at the consumer level because the retail price had not yet been adjusted downward from the wholesale discounting."
The cooperative collected temperature readings on a county-by-county basis from the early Sunday freeze and was analyzing the data to estimate total crop loss, he said.
"You can certainly say that this was a significant freeze, and the impact is going to be on the amount of total juice we will pack," he said.
Early Sunday, temperatures throughout central Florida fell to the low 20s for up to eight hours. Citrus can be damaged when temperatures fall below 28 degrees Fahrenheit for four hours or more.
